title: The Silk Road

source.name: Wikipedia — Silk Road
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: The Silk Road derives its name from the highly lucrative trade of silk textiles that were primarily produced in China. The network began with the expansion of the Han dynasty (202 BCE – 220 CE) into Central Asia around 114 BCE, through the missions and explorations of the Chinese imperial envoy Zhang Qian, which brought the region under unified control. The Chinese took great interest in the security of their trade products, and extended the Great Wall of China to ensure the protection of the trade route. The Parthian Empire provided a vital bridge connecting the network to the Mediterranean. Meanwhile, the rise of the Roman Empire in the west further established the western terminus of the interconnected trade system. By the first century CE, Chinese silk was widely sought after in Rome, Egypt, and Greece. Other lucrative commodities from the East included tea, dyes, perfumes, and porcelain; among Western exports were horses, camels, honey, wine, and gold. Aside from generating substantial wealth for emerging mercantile classes, the proliferation of goods such as paper and gunpowder greatly affected the trajectory of political history in several theatres in Eurasia and beyond.

The Silk Road was utilized over a period that saw immense political variation across the continent, exemplified by major events such as the Black Death and the Mongol conquests. The network was highly decentralized, and security was sparse: travelers faced constant threats of banditry and nomadic raiders, and long expanses of inhospitable terrain. Few individuals traveled the entire length of the Silk Road, instead relying on a succession of middlemen based at various stopping points along the way. In addition to goods, the network facilitated an unprecedented exchange of religious (especially Buddhist), philosophical, and scientific thought, much of which was syncretised by societies along the way. Likewise, a wide variety of people used the routes. Diseases such as plague also spread along the Silk Road, possibly contributing to the Black Death.

Despite the popular imagination, Silk Road was never a singular east-west trade route that linked China to the Mediterranean, nor was there unrestricted trade before the Mongol Empire. It was a network of routes. Even Marco Polo, often linked to the Silk Road, never used the term despite traveling during a time of Mongol-enabled ease of movement.

The use of the term 'Silk Road' is not without its detractors. For instance, Warwick Ball contends that the maritime spice trade with India and Arabia was far more consequential for the economy of the Roman Empire than the silk trade with China, which at sea was conducted mostly through India and on land was handled by numerous intermediaries such as the Sogdians. Going as far as to call the whole thing a "myth" of modern academia, Ball argues that there was no coherent overland trade system and no free movement of goods from East Asia to the West until the period of the Mongol Empire. He notes that traditional authors discussing east–west trade such as Marco Polo and Edward Gibbon never labelled any route a "silk" one in particular. William Dalrymple points out that in pre-modern times, maritime travel cost only a fifth of overland transport, and argues for the pre-13th century primacy of an India-dominated "Golden Road" extending from Rome to Japan.

questions.q: What does the text imply about the extension of the Great Wall?
options: It was paid for by merchants who wanted lower taxes
It was a way of connecting China with the Mediterranean
It was meant to protect the trade route and the goods on it
It was built to keep traders from the West out of China
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: người Trung Quốc quan tâm đến an ninh hàng hóa của mình và “extended the Great Wall… to ensure the protection of the trade route”.

questions.q: Why did few people travel the whole length of the Silk Road?
options: Goods mostly passed through middlemen, and the trip was dangerous
Governments allowed only soldiers to use the long routes
Silk was too heavy for travellers to carry across mountains
The road was closed to foreigners for most of its history
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: ít người đi hết chiều dài vì dựa vào “a succession of middlemen” ở các điểm dừng và vì nguy cơ cướp bóc, địa hình khắc nghiệt.

questions.q: Besides goods, what travelled along the network?
options: Religious and scientific ideas, and sometimes diseases too
Money that was collected in the form of taxes
Armies that were sent to protect important cities
Only sacred objects and teachers from one religion
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: ngoài hàng hóa còn có trao đổi tư tưởng tôn giáo (đặc biệt Phật giáo), triết học, khoa học; bệnh dịch như dịch hạch cũng lan theo.

questions.q: What does paragraph 3 say about the popular picture of the Silk Road?
options: It is misleading: there was a web of routes, and trade was limited before the Mongols
It is accurate, because Marco Polo described it in detail in his book
It is correct, because one single road joined China to the Mediterranean
It is outdated, because trade was completely free in all earlier centuries
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: “never a singular east-west trade route… nor was there unrestricted trade before the Mongol Empire. It was a network of routes.”

questions.q: According to Warwick Ball, which trade mattered more to the Roman economy?
options: The exchange of gold with merchants who lived in the eastern lands
The spice trade carried by ships across the Indian Ocean region
The trading of horses and camels with the peoples of Persia and Asia
Overland trade in silk textiles that came from the lands of China
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: Ball cho rằng thương mại gia vị đường biển với Ấn Độ và Ả Rập “far more consequential” cho kinh tế La Mã hơn tơ lụa.

questions.q: What does the word “detractors” in paragraph 4 suggest?
options: Several writers admired the work of Marco Polo and Gibbon
Merchants were against any form of trade between nations
Some scholars disagree with using the label “Silk Road” at all
Many travellers wrote about the dangers of the Silk Road
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: “The use of the term ‘Silk Road’ is not without its detractors” – có học giả phản đối cách dùng thuật ngữ này.

questions.q: Marco Polo used the term “Silk Road” in his writing.
questions.explain: Đoạn 3–4: Marco Polo “never used the term”.

questions.q: Silk was the most profitable product that was sold along the network.
questions.explain: Bài nói buôn bán lụa rất sinh lợi nhưng không so sánh mức lợi nhuận với các mặt hàng khác.

str.explain: Despite + danh từ: nhượng bộ, đối lập với điều thường nghĩ.

str.ex: nor was there unrestricted trade before the Mongol Empire
str.explain: Đảo ngữ sau nor: trợ động từ/be đứng trước chủ ngữ.

str.vi: Rất ít người …, mà dựa vào …
str.ex: Few individuals traveled the entire length of the Silk Road, instead relying on a succession of middlemen based at various stopping points along the way.
str.explain: few = gần như không có; instead + V-ing: thay vào đó.

str.vi: không phải không có người chỉ trích

str.explain: Phủ định kép (not without): nói giảm, nghĩa là “có khá nhiều người chỉ trích”.
